title: "6 Quantitative survey"
link-citations: true
---

Alternative labels: involving researchers and other interest-holders in health research

## Definition and features
In quantitative surveys, researchers use questionnaires to collect experiences, opinions, or feedback from larger samples of researchers and other interest-holders on methodological issues. They typically use random or stratified sampling to maximise representativeness. Researchers usually analyze responses quantitatively; for open-ended questions, they may first classify responses qualitatively and then analyze them quantitatively.

- A strength is possibillity to approach a large number of participants. 
- Key challenges include selection bias arising from low response rates and missing data.

## Typical purposes and corresponding examples 
[Assess needs and priorities for methods research](../purposes/5assess-needs-priorities.qmd): Survey to identify priorities for retention research;[@Kearney2017identifying] survey to identify priorities for methods research in the context of global health;[@Rosala-Hallas2018global] survey to identify solutions for the reproducibility crisis.[@Baker2016is] 

[Research the dissemination and implementation of methods](../purposes/13implementation.qmd): Survey of researchers to identify barriers to the implementation of new statistical methods.[@Pullenayegum2016knowledge]
